content: 1. The coadministration of certain antibiotics, such as cefepime/enmetazobactam, may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. This interaction is due to an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Cefepime/enmetazobactam can reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering its metabolism. This occurs because antibiotics can disrupt colonic bacterial flora, which is necessary for converting sodium picosulfate into its active form. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 3. Cefepime/enmetazobactam may increase the toxicity of streptomycin through mechanisms involving nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins, in general, can enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Close monitoring is essential. 4. Cefepime/enmetazobactam can reduce the effects of tislelizumab, toripalimab, and sintilimab, likely through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This may compromise the therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Cefepime/enmetazobactam can increase the toxicity of tobramycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may exacerbate the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Close monitoring is necessary. 6. Cefepime/enmetazobactam can reduce the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Live bacterial vaccines should be administered only after completing antibiotic treatment. 7. Cefepime/enmetazobactam may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination may also decrease prothrombin activity. Close monitoring of coagulation parameters is recommended, and exogenous vitamin K should be administered if indicated. 8. Adverse effects associated with cefepime include increased transaminases (20%), increased bilirubin (7%), headache (5%), phlebitis or infusion site reactions (5%), diarrhea (4%), anemia (3%), ALT > 3x ULN (3%), hypersensitivity (2%), AST > 3x ULN (2%), vomiting (2%), nausea (1%), and total bilirubin > 2x ULN. Other reported effects include eosinophilia, prolonged partial thromboplastin time (PTT), thrombocytopenia, eructation, Clostridioides difficile colitis, increased alkaline phosphatase, epistaxis, hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, dizziness, restlessness, increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and increased blood creatinine. 9. Serious adverse effects include agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, encephalopathy (manifesting as disturbances of consciousness, hallucinations, stupor, or coma), aphasia, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus, anaphylaxis (including anaphylactic shock), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme, toxic epidermal necrolysis, hepatic dysfunction (including cholestasis), renal dysfunction, toxic nephropathy, and hemorrhage. 10. Patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions to cefepime/enmetazobactam or other beta-lactam antibiotics should avoid these drugs. Cephalosporins, including cefepime, have been associated with decreased prothrombin activity. Prothrombin time should be monitored in at-risk patients (e.g., those with renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutritional status, or prolonged antibiotic courses). Exogenous vitamin K should be administered as needed. 11. The use of antibiotics in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to provide benefit and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 12. There is insufficient data on the use of cefepime/enmetazobactam or enmetazobactam during pregnancy to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Observational studies and case reports over several decades with cephalosporins, including cefepime, have not established drug-associated risks for these outcomes. 13. There is no available information on the effects of cefepime, enmetazobactam, or their combination on breastfed infants or milk production. 14. Cefepime/enmetazobactam solutions should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. The solution should appear clear to yellowish. 15.
